conventions.convention: Use Minkowski metric diag(-1,1,1,1), shell phase p∘x=p⁰x⁰−p⃗·x⃗, and massless measure d³k/((2π)³2|k|), omitting the null-measure apex.
Curve coordinates have length units; proper time has seconds; γ is smooth on a nonempty open interval, η(γ̇,γ̇)=−c², and γ̇⁰>|γ̇⃗|. Smearing tests have compact support inside that interval.
The Hilbert pairing is second-variable-linear; distribution pairings are bilinear without conjugating the test. The angular Fourier kernel is exp(−iνs), with inverse factor 1/(2π).

The accelerated spectral assertions retain conditional reliance on the draft contour-spectrum and exponential-current suppliers. The length-coordinate conversion is α=a/c², u=cs, and C_a(s)=C_α(cs)/π.
The switch h is real, smooth, compactly supported and nonzero; duration is strictly positive. The normalized coefficient divides by duration times ||h||₂².

The separately defined two-state model orders states (g,e), uses row distributions π=(1−p,p), and evolves by π′=πQ with Q=[[-r₊,r₊],[r₋,−r₋]]. Rates are adopted model inputs, not exact QFT transition probabilities.
Countable Choice is assumed throughout the constructed field, Fourier, and switched-coefficient results.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming Countable Choice and the stated massless shell and Fock conventions, every compact smooth test along a smooth future-directed proper-time timelike curve has shell amplitude K_γf in H₀, continuously on fixed-support test spaces. Real tests define a symmetric finite-particle field with self-adjoint closure and covariance ⟨K_γf,K_γg⟩₂. For the specified hyperbola with a>0, the covariance is C_a(s)=−a² csch²(a(s−i0)/(2c))/(16π²c⁴). Conditional on the stated draft suppliers, S_a(ν)=ν/[2πc²(exp(2πcν/a)−1)], with S_a(0)=a/(4π²c³) and S_a(−ν)=exp(2πcν/a)S_a(ν) for ν>0. The inertial comparison is C₀(s)=−1/[4π²c²(s−i0)²] and S₀(ν)=max(−ν,0)/(2πc²).

Assume Countable Choice and the preceding covariance/spectrum pairs, retaining the conditional accelerated input. For real nonzero h∈C_c∞(R), duration T>0, and either pair, K_h=(2π||h||₂²)⁻¹∫|z||ĥ(z)|²dz is finite, R_T(ν)=T²/(2π)∫S(ω)|ĥ(T(ν−ω))|²dω≥0, and |R_T(ν)/(T||h||₂²)−S(ν)|≤Lip(S)K_h/T for every real ν. For the separately defined two-state model with positive E, ℏ, k_B and γ_d, r₊=γ_dS_a(E/ℏ) and r₋=γ_dS_a(−E/ℏ), every initial p(0)∈[0,1] gives p(t)=p_*+(p(0)−p_*)exp(−(r₊+r₋)t) for t≥0, where p_*=1/(1+exp(2πcE/(aℏ))) and the defined effective temperature is ℏa/(2πck_B).

concerns.concern: The Statement attributes hyperbolic conventions to lem-tgr-exponential-current and says “that item also states sinh′=cosh and cosh′=sinh.” The current supplier does not explicitly state both derivative identities; its Statement defines Y_b using sinh and gives Y_b′=cosh. The identities used here follow immediately by differentiating the locally displayed exponential formulas, so this is a citation-description issue rather than a defect in the calculation.

seams_checked.note: Checked the positive-damping, exponential-current, and contour-spectrum arguments. The consumer uses the contour Statement's chiral specialization with α=a/c² and u=cs. The covariance factor 1/π and Fourier factor 1/(πc) give exactly the displayed accelerated spectrum, zero value, and detailed balance. Draft status and conditional reliance are preserved.

The adopting postulate and acceleration theorem use the constructed temporal smear, the conditional accelerated spectrum, and the finite-switch coefficient estimate faithfully. They retain the draft-supplier qualifications and separately adopted rate equation, without claiming exact QFT transition probabilities or empirical readings. The reduced-branch theorem does not strengthen these batch-75 results.
